source.title: Two open problems in precedence constrained scheduling

accepted.question_text: Determine the computational complexity of the following optimization problem. There are n jobs, all available at time 0, to be processed nonpreemptively on a single machine. Every job has unit processing time, and each job j has an integer due date d_j. The precedence constraints are chain-like: in the directed precedence graph on the jobs, each vertex has indegree at most one and outdegree at most one. A feasible schedule is a permutation σ of the jobs that respects the precedence constraints, meaning σ(j) < σ(k) whenever (j,k) is a precedence arc. If job j is scheduled in position σ(j), then its tardiness is max(0, σ(j) - d_j). What is the complexity of finding a precedence-feasible schedule minimizing the total tardiness over all jobs?
accepted.context_brief: single-machine total tardiness with chain-like precedence

accepted.question_text: Determine the computational complexity of the following optimization problem. There are n jobs, all of unit processing time, to be processed nonpreemptively on a single machine. Each job j has an integer due date d_j and a release date r_j, so job j is unavailable before time r_j. The precedence constraints are chain-like: in the directed precedence graph on the jobs, each vertex has indegree at most one and outdegree at most one. A feasible schedule must respect both the release dates and the precedence arcs, and if job j completes at time C_j then its tardiness is max(0, C_j - d_j). What is the complexity of finding a feasible schedule minimizing the total tardiness over all jobs?
accepted.context_brief: single-machine total tardiness with chain-like precedence and release dates

accepted.question_text: Determine the computational complexity of the following optimization problem. The input is a directed precedence graph G on n unit-time jobs to be scheduled on three identical parallel machines. A feasible schedule assigns each job j to an integer time slot σ(j) in such a way that σ(j) < σ(k) whenever (j,k) is a precedence arc of G, and at most three jobs are assigned to any one time slot. The objective is to minimize the makespan, that is, the largest occupied time slot. What is the complexity of finding this minimum makespan?
